statement: Never git add -A, git add ., or git commit -a in this repo; stage by explicit path and commit with git commit --only, and for partial-file staging (git apply --cached / git add -p) commit immediately after with no other commands in between
rationale: This repo's shared clone hosts multiple parallel Claude Code sessions on main at once. git commit <pathspec> is shorthand for --only against the WORKING TREE at those exact paths, not "my hunks" — it re-sweeps a sibling session's uncommitted edits in the same file. For genuinely partial-hunk staging where --only can't be used, the safe pattern is git apply --cached (stage only the intended hunk) followed immediately by a bare git commit with no commands between, minimizing the race window.
